title: Concept Drills — Literature: Essays, Plays (Class 11 English)
subject: english

questions.question: 'War' is a topic; what is a theme? Give a theme for a war story in one sentence.
questions.solution: A topic is the subject (war); a theme is the CLAIM the text makes about it — a complete idea, e.g. 'war destroys the moral compass of ordinary soldiers'. Themes are statements, not single words; one-word answers lose marks.

questions.question: Why does a personal essay feel different from a report on the same subject?
questions.solution: A personal essay filters the subject through the writer's EXPERIENCE, opinion and style — anecdotes, humour, reflection — making the reader connect with a mind, not just information. A report strips the self out for objectivity. Voice is the essay's signature; its absence makes prose forgettable.

questions.question: Define dramatic irony and explain why it makes an audience feel powerful rather than confused.
questions.solution: Dramatic irony: the AUDIENCE knows something a character does not (we have seen the villain plotting; the character trusts him). The gap creates suspense and a feeling of privileged insight — we watch the character walk toward what we foresee. It is a structural device for tension, not confusion, because the playwright deliberately gave us the knowledge.

questions.question: How can a playwright reveal character without any narration?
questions.solution: Through DIALOGUE and STAGE DIRECTIONS: what a character says, how they say it (formal, slangy, evasive), what others say about them, and the actions the directions specify (pauses, exits, props). Every word a character speaks is self-characterisation — the audience infers personality from speech and behaviour alone.

questions.question: What makes a literary paragraph persuasive rather than mere opinion?
questions.solution: The chain: claim → evidence (a short quotation or concrete detail) → analysis (how the evidence supports the claim) → link back to the thesis. 'The story is sad' asserts; 'The writer's image of the empty cradle shows…' demonstrates with proof and mechanism. Quoted evidence plus explanation is the examinable structure.
